newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - British shares end at record despite caution.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - British shares end at record despite caution.

text.p: British shares soared to their third record close in a row on Thursday, spurred on by a sizzling hot U.S. share market and the belief that interest rates will remain low -- at least for now.

The FTSE 100 index of British blue chip shares finished 39.2 points higher at 4,399.3, surpassing the old record of 4,360.1 set just 24 hours before. Earlier, the index broke above 4,400 for the first time, hitting an intraday record of 4,402.7.

But many of Britain's top stockbrokers were not ready to pop champagne corks just yet as they fear the share market's bubbly performance, which has seen the FTSE 100 jump around seven percent this year and over 40 percent since 1995, could be about to burst.
"The market is nervous. Everybody knows that the Dow is going to have a correction," the head of share trading at a large U.S. brokerage in London said.
"The only questions to be answered at the moment are when will the Dow correction start and how far will we follow it down," the dealer said.

Share investors fear the U.S. share market, which has virtually defied gravity by jumping more than 75 percent in the past two years alone, could be about to cool down -- an event which would almost certainly take the heat out of British shares.
The Dow Industrials Average of the 30 leading U.S. shares, which rocketed 93 points on Wednesday, was up another 35 points by the time the London market closed.

Both the U.S. and British share markets have been supported by the current low interest rate environment which encourages investors to put their hard-earned cash in shares, which historically offer a higher rate of return than bank or building society accounts.

But some stockbrokers fear interest rates on both sides of the Atlantic, which are at their lowest levels in 30 years, will be pushed up in the next few months in order to prevent a return of inflation and the "boom and bust" economic cycle that comes with it.
Some believe that the catalyst for both an interest rate increase and a fall in share prices could be Friday's U.S. unemployment report.
If the monthly survey shows U.S. wages are rising and that the jobless rate is falling, the U.S. Federal Reserve may be tempted to try and take the steam out of the red-hot U.S. economy.
"If they see any signs that inflation is coming through they've got to raise rates to stop it," a share trader at a British stockbrokers said.

Among individual shares, British drugs giant Glaxo Wellcome was the most active FTSE constituent, with over 24 million shares traded after the company told analysts it would return to double-digit sales growth by the end of the century.
The company also reported an 18 percent rise in pre-tax profit to 2.96 billion pounds.

Chocolate maker Cadbury posted strong gains in active trade on continued reaction to Wednesday's good results. The shares closed up 11-1/2p to 540-1/2 after the company promised a greater focus on shareholder value.

Jet engine maker Rolls-Royce Plc was another big gainer, adding 16-1/2p to close at 255-1/2 after the group posted slightly better than expected underlying profits and raised the dividend payout for the first time since 1992.
